1qg20m0:226: GrowLoop's "double-loop" design — a scoring-rubric iteration loop and a test-question evolution loop — is a deep application of Harness Engineering thinking to evaluation. In the second loop, the converged rubrics are used to generate new questions (500 items), which must pass 5 quality gates (distribution divergence, model discriminability, tier gaps, headroom reservation, etc.). After sampling, human annotators label new seeds, triggering another round of rubric learning.

mz07yc:244: GrowLoop adopts the Heuristic Learning paradigm, letting large models externalize tacit knowledge through metacognitive reflection. Specifically, instead of fitting annotators' score distributions, the model reflects on why its own judgments differ from the annotators'. This reflection process externalizes the scoring rationale that even annotators themselves cannot articulate — for example, "being verbose under time pressure is itself a mistake" — into structured scoring anchors. The significance of this mechanism goes beyond dialogue evaluation: it reveals the unique value of large models in knowledge externalization. Large models can act as "optimizers at the language level" (an extension of the TextGrad paradigm to evaluation), making tacit knowledge explicit.
pjmxxj:157: The elegance of this design is that rubrics and test questions drive each other to grow together, rather than being optimized independently. Rubrics produce better questions; good questions expose blind spots in the rubrics; blind spots then drive rubric evolution. This co-evolution mechanism resolves the fundamental contradiction of static evaluation schemes — "standards themselves become outdated." As AI capabilities improve and user expectations shift, scoring standards must keep updating, and GrowLoop provides a systematic methodological framework for doing so.
